clue.text: Informed about particular caper as one is arising, very early

definitions.text: as one is arising, very early

parts.note: to be up with something is to be informed about it, abreast of it
the definite article points to one particular thing
a lark is a caper, a bit of fun or mischief

explanation.surface: Someone well briefed on a certain prank, getting out of bed at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Informed about' makes UP WITH as a single phrase, as in keeping up with the news; the rest builds on it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means rising at dawn, when the skylark begins singing, so it describes someone getting up very early.

clue.text: I fear the worst, as I fail to catch up — nuisance about that

indicators.note: about means going round, so the nuisance word surrounds the rest

parts.note: a pest is a nuisance, an annoying person

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the pieces are read bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to miss a ball or a train is to fail to catch it

explanation.surface: A gloomy confession from someone who keeps missing the bus and is pestered by a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns I + MISS into SSIMI, and 'about' puts that inside PEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who always expects the worst outcome is a person of gloomy outlook, here speaking in the first person.

clue.text: Indium and vanadium are not finally needed for this alloy

parts.note: In is the chemical symbol for indium
V is the chemical symbol for vanadium

indicators.note: not finally tells us to drop the last letter of the word are

explanation.surface: A chemistry note listing what goes into a particular alloy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not finally' removes the E from ARE, leaving AR.
explanation.definitionFit: Invar is a nickel-iron alloy prized for barely expanding with heat, used in clocks and instruments.

clue.text: Playing Bath, you suggest what was played before

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are toyed with and rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark about a play put on in Bath and what was staged earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' rearranges BATH and YOU. The definition is fair because the hautboy is the old name for an oboe, an instrument played in earlier centuries.
explanation.definitionFit: The hautboy is the historical woodwind instrument from which the modern oboe developed, so it was played in times past.

clue.text: Broken toy-half found somewhere in a barn

indicators.note: broken signals that the letters are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: Half of a broken toy turns up somewhere in a barn.
explanation.definitionFit: A hayloft is the upper storage floor of a barn where fodder is kept.

clue.text: Lord acquires estate, about to set up in Welsh community

indicators.note: acquires means the lord word takes in the estate word

parts.note: lud is a form of lord, as in the courtroom address m'lud
land is an estate, property in the country

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means read upwards, so the word is turned backwards

parts.note: on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A nobleman buys property and is about to establish himself in a Welsh town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acquires' puts LAND inside LUD, giving LLANDUD; 'set up' turns ON into NO. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Llandudno is a seaside resort town on the north coast of Wales.

clue.text: Villain's accent ignored at first

indicators.note: ignored at first tells us the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: a brogue is an accent, especially an Irish one

explanation.surface: A villain's way of speaking is overlooked at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignored at first' drops the B of BROGUE. The 's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest scoundrel, a synonym for a villain.

clue.text: Edge towards slips? Unlikely prospect

definitions.meaning: in cricket, an outside edge off the bat flies to the slip fielders and may give a catch

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the slips are fielders standing beside the wicketkeeper, waiting for balls that clip the outer edge of the bat.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a cricket edge that may offer a catch, and a slim possibility of success.

clue.text: Perk up in Edinburgh?

parts.note: a perk is an extra benefit of a job; the Edinburgh festival has its famous alternative arts strand, so a perk there sounds like a festival bonus

explanation.walkthrough: The Edinburgh Fringe is the huge open arts festival held alongside the Edinburgh International Festival each August.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra advantage given with a job beyond salary, a perk, with a nod to the Edinburgh festival.

clue.text: One sort of cabbage you are told to stuff is tasteless

parts.note: 'un is a colloquial form of one, as in a good 'un

indicators.note: to stuff means to be packed inside the cabbage word

parts.note: the savoy is a variety of cabbage with crinkled leaves

indicators.note: told means spoken, so we use the letters that sound like the words

parts.note: said aloud, you are sounds like the letters U and R

explanation.surface: Being told to stuff a cabbage with something is a distasteful instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'told' turns 'you are' into UR, the letters sounding like it, and 'to stuff' puts UR inside SAVOY.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsavoury means unpleasant or lacking in flavour, so it can stand for tasteless.

clue.text: Get annoyed, and risk daughter leaving

indicators.note: leaving means that letter departs from the word

parts.note: danger is risk, peril

explanation.surface: Someone gets cross and takes a chance after their daughter walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' removes D from DANGER. 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Used without an object, the verb means to become cross or irritated, as in 'he is slow to rouse'.

clue.text: Shot high into air? I may have!

definitions.text: Shot high into air? I may have!

parts.words: Shot high into air? I may have!
parts.note: a cricket shot that goes steeply up is named after a slope sportsman, and a ski jumper may also be shot high into the air

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a ball hit almost straight up is called a skier; the speaker 'I' is a ski jumper launched off the ramp.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a ball struck high upward in cricket, and a person on skis who might fly into the air.

clue.text: Comprehensive head served vegetable

parts.note: broad means comprehensive, wide-ranging
bean is slang for the head

explanation.surface: A comprehensive school head serves up the vegetables at lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comprehensive' looks like a British state school, but it means BROAD. 'served' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The broad bean is a large flat edible legume grown in gardens.

clue.text: Such habits involve no pressing needs

definitions.text: Such habits involve no pressing needs

parts.words: Such habits involve no pressing needs
parts.note: habits here are clothes, and pressing means ironing: garments that need no ironing after washing

explanation.walkthrough: 'habits' suggests routines and 'pressing needs' urgent ones, but habits are garments and pressing is ironing.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes fabric that dries smooth when hung up wet, so it needs no ironing.

clue.text: The same glue flaking holds everything up in Welsh town

parts.note: do is short for ditto, meaning the same

indicators.note: holds means the rearranged glue letters contain the other piece
flaking glue breaks apart, so its letters are rearranged
in a down clue, up means read backwards from bottom to top

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: The same glue keeps peeling off and holding everything up in a Welsh town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flaking' rearranges GLUE to LGEU, 'up' turns ALL into LLA, and 'holds' puts LLA inside: LGE-LLA-U.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolgellau is a market town in Gwynedd, north-west Wales.

clue.text: Naturally, one can make a jumper eventually

definitions.text: Naturally, one can make a jumper eventually

parts.words: Naturally, one can make a jumper eventually
parts.note: a jumper is not knitwear but a frog, which a young larva grows into in nature

explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' suggests the British word for a sweater, but here it is a leaping animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tadpole is the larval stage of a frog, which eventually matures into the hopping adult.

clue.text: Where poultice may be applied, steaming

definitions.meaning: a poultice is a warm dressing placed on a skin swelling such as a boil

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: placed upon an abscess, and at boiling point or in full swing.

clue.text: Family receiving a thank-you from Spain?

indicators.note: receiving means the family word takes the other letters in

parts.note: a clan is a family group
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: A family gets a thank-you note from Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiving' puts A + TA inside CLAN. The question mark flags that Catalonia is one region of Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Catalan describes something from Catalonia, the north-eastern region of Spain.

clue.text: Don't cut copy held up where there's a memo?

indicators.note: held means the reworked letters contain the other piece
cut means shuffled like a deck of cards, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of the word don't, apostrophe ignored

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read backwards

parts.note: to ape is to copy, imitate

explanation.surface: An instruction not to trim a document that has been delayed, on the page where a memo sits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut', as with a pack of cards, rearranges DONT into NOTD; 'up' turns APE into EPA; 'held' puts EPA inside: NOT-EPA-D.
explanation.definitionFit: A pad of paper for jotting messages is where a written reminder would be found.

clue.text: Hector left with a flourish and a laugh

indicators.note: with a flourish suggests a showy rearrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Hector made a theatrical exit, laughing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a flourish' rearranges HECTOR plus L. 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A chortle is a gleeful chuckle, a kind of laugh.

clue.text: Almost ring agent over old song

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent

explanation.surface: A secret agent nearly phones about an old tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims CALL to CAL; 'over' turns SPY into YPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A calypso is a West Indian style of song, often topical and witty.

clue.text: Supplying food, a form of North American millet

indicators.note: a form of means the letters are reshaped into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Providing nourishment with a North American variety of millet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' rearranges A, NA and MILLET together.
explanation.definitionFit: Alimental means nourishing, relating to aliment, which is food.

clue.text: Where Turks are involved in showbiz miracle

indicators.note: involved in means the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Turkish people take part in a show-business marvel.
explanation.definitionFit: Izmir is a large port city on Turkey's Aegean coast, home to many Turks.

clue.text: Note word over page, finally

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a verb is a part of speech, a kind of word

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of page

explanation.surface: A note says to turn the page over to the last word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns VERB into BREV.
explanation.definitionFit: A breve is a long musical note worth two semibreves.

clue.text: Tree worker's seen near church

parts.note: a bee, particularly a worker bee, is a typical crossword worker

explanation.surface: A labourer spotted near a church among the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 's seen near' is a link: the BEE is placed beside CH.
explanation.definitionFit: The beech is a common broadleaf woodland tree with smooth grey bark.

clue.text: Animal approached lake

parts.note: came means approached, drew near

explanation.surface: A creature came up to the edge of a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The camel is a humped desert mammal.

clue.text: Pizza topping? Go for every possible one!

parts.note: pep means go, energy
per means for every, as in per head
on means possible, feasible, as in that's not on
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An order to pick every possible option from the pizza toppings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possible' gives ON in its sense of feasible ('that's just not on').
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is a spicy salami sausage commonly sliced on pizzas.

clue.text: Reason tiny kid running round a prince slowly stopped?

parts.note: ground means reason, as in grounds for complaint

indicators.note: running round means the child word goes round the other letters

parts.note: a tot is a tiny child
Hal is Prince Hal, Shakespeare's young Henry V

explanation.surface: A small child runs circles round a prince until they are worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running round' puts A + HAL inside TOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To grind to a halt is to come gradually to a standstill, here in the past tense.
